question: Should OpenClaw accept this staged `claws apply --yes` provenance/ref-accounting contract as the first mutating Claws slice after the duplicate entry-id collision is fixed?
rationale: The patch creates public CLI behavior and persistent artifact ownership state that future installers and removers will inherit, so automation cannot choose the long-term product and security contract.

options.title: Fix Then Approve Contract
options.body: Require duplicate entry-id protection plus explicit approval of the mutating CLI, SQLite tables, and ownership semantics before merge.

options.title: Accept Staged Contract Risk
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally merge after acknowledging that later installer and remove semantics will be constrained by this state model.

options.title: Pause Until RFC/Base Settle
options.body: Keep this draft paused until the base Claws PR and RFC lock down the lifecycle surface.

recommendation.title: Fix Then Approve Contract
recommendation.body: Require duplicate entry-id protection plus explicit approval of the mutating CLI, SQLite tables, and ownership semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest routing owner for a new core CLI and persistent-state product contract.
